title: Foreign Language Glossary with Print Colon

illustrates.quote: f. When a print colon and a subentry word, rather than a translation, are shown following the entry word, substitute a semicolon for the colon. Place the subentry word on the following braille line at the established margin. The translation follows on the next braille line indented two cells to the right of the established margin.

blocks.text:
to show enseñar, 4; to show photos enseñar fotos, 9
shy tímido(a), 2
sick: to be estar enfermo(a), 7
silk la seda, 8
silly tonto(a), 3
blocks.features: Entry words are aligned vertically. The English infinitive 'to' hangs in the left margin. Same not-representable margin-alignment class as Example 21-36 (F-193/F-199).

print.notes: In print, 'show', 'shy', 'sick', 'silk', and 'silly' are vertically aligned. The 'to ' before 'show' hangs to the left. The braille for the 'sick: to be' entry does not strictly follow the second sentence of the rule (it does not place 'to be' on its own following braille line).
print.printFeatures: Hanging indent for English infinitive 'to'. Print colon used in the 'sick' entry.

braille.notes: Re-extracted from source: the given run's braille.lines both wrongly included the 'Example 21-37: ...' title/blank lines AND failed to strip this file's own 9-space left margin from every real content line (the only file among all 39 examples where the margin strip was skipped entirely) — both corrected. Corrected per BANA foreign-language changes June 2024 (below); the 'sick: to be' entry still does not apply 21.9.2e (margins), as in the book.

resolution: braille.lines corrected: removed 5 bogus leading lines AND stripped the 9-space left margin that the given run had left in place on every real content line (a transcription bug unique to this file).

corrections.note: New rule 21.9.2c: where print has no punctuation after an entry word, leave two blank cells instead of a braille colon. The 'sick: to be' entry keeps its semicolon (sick2) because print DOES show a colon there (rule f/21.9.2f, substitute semicolon for print colon); only the unpunctuated 'to be'/translation join changes to two cells.
